title: Improve INT8/FP8 quantized kernels: smoothquant weight folding + dequant-fusion + KV-cache-aware batching
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Performance: Improved quantized INT8/FP8 kernel throughput and latency via fused dequant+matmul and smoothquant weight folding. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers running quantized inference (INT8/FP8) reported suboptimal throughput when the runtime had to perform dequantize->matmul->quantize roundtrips, especially for transformer workloads with short prefixes and heavy KV-cache reuse. This PR implements a set of runtime kernel and scheduling changes to reduce per-token overhead and improve batch utilization while preserving numerical parity for common workloads.

What this PR does (summary):
- New fused dequantize+matmul kernel (dequant_fused_gemm) that consumes INT8/FP8 weights and produces FP32/FP16 outputs without an intermediate full dequant buffer. Reduces memory traffic and kernel launch overhead.
- SmoothQuant weight folding pass applied at model load time: precomputes per-channel scale adjustments and folds into the quantized weight layout to improve accuracy of pure INT8 runs.
- Dequant-fusion fallback paths for FP8 models: when model uses FP8 storage we use a fast path that keeps computation in FP8/FP16 pointer-arithmetic and only expands to FP32 at accumulation points.
- KV-cache-aware batching scheduler adjustments: coalesces small requests that share prefix KV keys and executes fused kernels across coalesced batches to increase GEMM utilization without violating latency SLOs.
- Micro-optimizations: reduced memcpy footprint in KV cache hot-path, aligned weight tensors for AVX512/WMMA, and improved thread-affinity hints for NUMA-balanced execution.

Changes included: code changes span runtime/quant, runtime/scheduling, runtime/kvcache, and runtime/benchmarks. All changes are backward-compatible at the API level. Internal config knobs (--quant-fuse, --smoothquant-enable, --kvcache-coalesce-threshold) are behind feature flags for gradual rollout.

Testing and verification: unit tests for kernel correctness (randomized property-based tests), deterministic FP32 golden comparisons, end-to-end inference tests using GPT-small and Llama-7B quantized artifacts, and a benchmark suite comparing baseline vs this PR across sequence lengths (16/64/256) and batch sizes (1/8/16). Performance validation was run on NVIDIA A100 and H100 hardware.

Risk/compatibility: SmoothQuant folding is optional; enabled for QA runs only. The fused kernels are guarded by hardware capability checks and fall back to existing code paths when unsupported. No public API changes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel unit tests added
- [x] Benchmarks recorded and attached
- [x] Reviewed by runtime and SRE
- [x] Feature flags added for controlled rollout

Related: ENG-4829 (quant perf epic), ENG-4912 (kvcache scheduling), SUP-1203 (customer incident describing dequant overhead).

testing_notes:
Benchmarks (A100, fp32 baseline vs this PR):
- seq=16, batch=1: throughput +1.6x, p50 latency -18%
- seq=64, batch=8: throughput +1.8x, p50 latency -22%
- seq=256, batch=16: throughput +1.5x, p50 latency -12%
FP8 fallback path: average latency improvement ~15% vs previous FP8 path. Accuracy: <0.5% perplexity delta on GPT-small eval after smoothquant folding when using INT8.
Regression tests: 1200 unit tests, 45 integration scenarios, 10 perf suites. Bench artifacts uploaded to: /artifacts/quant-pr-324567/
notes: Rollout plan: enable behind flags for Dedicated customers for 2 weeks, monitor per-route token latency and RV metrics, then flip default for hosted API if no regressions. Coordinate with SRE for canary on one region.
